comments.body: There are some considerations on the platform that may apply here. Binding to specific sockets from 0-1024 are restricted to root only. I cannot change that. This applies to both UDP and TCP. I am wondering whether that is the cause of both errors above.

It seems unlikely since the same restrictions apply to Linux.

The failing of the dgram_pair test is curious since that is an in-memory BIO and doesn't do anything with OS sockets.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I threw this into `gdb` at `BIO_socket`. The failing call is resolved to `socket(AF_INET6, SOCK_DGRAM, 17)`, which normally should work. It appears that IPv6 is not configured on the box I am using for testing, so we are getting `EAFNOSUPPORT`. Perhaps we need to add a check and bypass the test if IPv6 is not enabled (help is requested for doing this if we need to). I am urgently working with the sysadmin to get this changed as it seems to be hitting multiple tests.

**Note:** It may take a week or two to get this changed because this is a shared system and I have to give lots of notice for this type of configuration change to the IP stack. Would that cause problems for other pull requests that might result to get this into 3.2.0-beta?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Nonetheless — I think this is a bug if our code is breaking without IPv6.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Yeah, we absolutely must support non-IPv6 boxes. They are still common.

comments.body: Wasn't @participant1 looking at similar IPv6 issues on VMS? Is this the same as those?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> Wasn't @participant1 looking at similar IPv6 issues on VMS? Is this the same as those?

I do not think it is the same problem - in @participant1's case the IPv6 support was AFAIK completely non-present on the VMS builder, but there was still some attempt to resolve IPv6 addresses. However here the IPv6 support is enabled in headers, etc. so this builds with IPv6 support, but IPv6 is not configured, so the tests using IPv6 will fail.

So IMO completely different issue. We might want to try to configure a VM without IPv6 to test this.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> sizeof(hdr)=2064

!!!! Oh wow! That's huge! This is the cause of the problem. On my system this value is 232.

This is the line in the test that is failing:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/84f371a130dbe7a46595fbabd274f152a0e6385f/test/bio_dgram_test.c#L561-L566

The default write buffer size is 17408. Each datagram consists of a random length up to the max mtu of 1472 plus the datagram header (2064 bytes in your case).

On my system, in the worst case scenario where every datagram has the maximum length, this means we could fit `17408 / (1472 + 232) == 10.2` datagrams into the default buffer size. This test conservatively assumes that we should be able to fit at least 9 in.

But on your system the test is failing with:

````
        # ERROR: (int) 'i >= 9' failed @ /home/<user>/openssl/test/bio_dgram_test.c:565
        # [6] compared to [9]
````

i.e. it only managed to fit 6 datagrams in. This seems about right. If the average datagram length is half the mtu (736). Then each datagram plus the header is `736+2064 == 2800`. With the buffer size of 17408 we can fit `17408 / 2064 == 6.2`.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
The hdr struct is defined here:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/e22ebb893e2f44bd08f69f9ce4ccfc5e4d2990e2/crypto/bio/bss_dgram_pair.c#L243-L246

I assume it is `sizeof(BIO_ADDR)` which is larger than expected (perhaps 1000 bytes assuming `sizeof(size_t)` is 64??)

a `BIO_ADDR` is simply a union containing these things:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/e22ebb893e2f44bd08f69f9ce4ccfc5e4d2990e2/include/internal/bio_addr.h#L16-L27

Where all of those types are defined by the system. It's very strange that they are so large on Non-stop!

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> NO_UNIX_SOCK

I think this might break access to PRNGD, which is accessed via UNIX sockets. Going through TCP is an option, but a painful one. We only use PRNGD on ia64, not x86, though.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant4 to clarify, this particular issue is closed as resolved. In order to work on your situation, we need a new case opened, with details about how you built the code and the errors you are seeing - they may be the same or different, but the configuration is crucial. Use the following command at the highest directory in your clone (probably `openssl`):
```
perl configdata.pm --dump
```
That will tell the team how you built the code. Also, please send the output of the following command:
```
git show --oneline -s
```
which will show the commit you are using for the build. Also include the errors.

Please do this using the `New Issue` button from the `Issues` tab in the `openssl/openssl` repository.
